drivingQuestion: In the mishna's two disputes about imprecise enunciation and inaudible recitation, whose view is the halakha?
outcomeNote: The ruling's word שניהם (both) has no referent inside this unit; it points to the two disputes cited in berakhot.sugya124.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי טָבִי אָמַר רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה: הֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי שְׁנֵיהֶם לְהָקֵל.
segments.en: «Rabbi Tavi said» that «Rabbi Yoshiya said: The halakha is in accordance with» «the statements in both» disputes that rule «leniently».

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי טבי אמר רבי יאשיה: הלכה כדברי שניהם להקל
moves.summary: R' Yoshiya, reported by R' Tavi, rules leniently in both of the mishna's disputes
moves.about: in the dispute over imprecise enunciation the halakha follows the lenient view, which is R' Yosei's

edges.cueHe: אמר רבי טבי אמר רבי יאשיה
edges.about: R' Tavi reports R' Yoshiya's halakhic ruling on the two disputes of the mishna
in the dispute over imprecise enunciation the halakha follows the lenient view, which is R' Yosei's
in the dispute over reciting inaudibly the halakha follows the lenient view, which is the first tanna's

extras.about: R' Tavi reports R' Yoshiya's halakhic ruling on the two disputes of the mishna
